Day 3 · Monday 24 May 2027 · Dress code: Black Tie

STAVANGER

Old Town, Colour Street + Lysefjord

OLD TOWN • FJORD VIEWS • MUSEUMS • SEAFOOD • STREET ART

WALK STRAIGHT OFF THE SHIP INTO THE CITY CENTRE

HistoryFjordsFoodColourCulture

Where the ship docks

  • Ships berth inside Vågen, the central harbour. The main quay, Strandkaien, takes the biggest ships and sits right below the Old Town.
  • No tender needed in most cases, and no big terminal: you step through a simple gate and you are in town.
  • Tourist information is at Strandkaien 61, between the ships and the Old Town, with excursions from around 30 operators.
  • On the busiest days a ship can be sent to an outer berth about 1 km north (a 10–15 minute walk).

Can you walk?

  • Yes. The centre is flat and compact, and nothing that matters is more than about 10 minutes from any central quay.
  • From Strandkaien the Old Town is about a 5-minute walk up a gentle cobbled rise.
  • The cathedral, fish market, Colour Street and Petroleum Museum are all walkable.
  • Pulpit Rock is not walkable: it is about 1 hour each way by bus, plus a 4-hour hike.
  • The hop-on hop-off bus leaves from the cruise terminal: about 55 minutes a loop, every 30 minutes.

Stavanger
at a glance

  • Gamle Stavanger~5 min walk
  • Fish Marketon the quay
  • Fargegaten~5–10 min
  • Cathedralshort walk
  • Petroleum Museum~5–10 min
  • Pulpit Rock~1 hr by bus

  • Be at the pier 20 min early

  • Only if your call is long
  • Book the ship's tour for peace of mind

Day 4 · Tuesday 25 May 2027 · Dress code: Evening Casual

OLDEN

Glaciers, Skylift + Turquoise Lakes

GLACIERS • CABLE CAR • LAKES • WATERFALLS • VILLAGE WALKS

ONE BIG CHOICE: BRIKSDAL GLACIER OR THE LOEN SKYLIFT

GlaciersMountainsLakesViewsPeace

Where the ship docks

  • Ships dock at Olden Cruise Pier, a deep-water berth at the head of the Nordfjord.
  • No tender needed for most ships; the gangway leads straight to the pier.
  • A small terminal has tourist info, tour operators and souvenir stalls.
  • If a second ship is in port, one may anchor and tender, so check the daily programme.

Can you walk?

  • Yes. The village is about 1 km away: a flat 10–15 minute walk along the fjord.
  • The walk brings you to the churches, shops and the Oldeelva glacial river.
  • The big sights are not walkable: Loen Skylift is about 6 km away and Briksdal Glacier about 25 km.
  • A land train runs a 70-minute tour, and RIB and kayak trips leave from near the pier.
  • Taxis are scarce. Book shuttles or excursions in advance.

Olden
at a glance

  • Olden village~15 min walk
  • Old Church (1759)~15 min walk
  • Loen Skylift~10 min drive
  • Lovatnet Lakeshort drive
  • Briksdal Glacier~30–45 min drive
  • Huaren viewpointsteep hike

Popular excursions
(from your booking options)

1Olden Village

Olden Village
  • Flat 1 km walk from the pier

Olden Old Church

3Briksdal Glacier

  • Arm of Jostedalsbreen, mainland Europe's largest glacier
  • About 25 km up the Oldedalen valley
  • Walk past the Kleivafossen waterfall

4Loen Skylift

  • One of the world's steepest cable cars
  • Climbs to 1,011 m in about 5 minutes
  • Restaurant at the top of Mount Hoven
  • Huge views over the Nordfjord
  • About 2–3 hours door to door

5Lovatnet Lake

  • Turquoise glacial lake
  • About 11 km long
  • Leads to the Kjenndal glacier
  • Quieter than Briksdal
  • Coffee stop at the lodge

6Fjord RIB, Kayak or SUP

  • Start from the dock
  • See cliffs, waterfalls and farms
  • Splash gear provided on RIBs
  • Calm water for paddling
  • 1–2 hours

7Huaren Viewpoint

Huaren Viewpoint
  • Free but steep hike
  • About 4 km return, 1.5–2 hours
  • Climbs to roughly 400 m
  • Look down on the ship
  • Only for confident hikers

8Stryn & Nordfjord

  • Regional town about 16 km away
  • Lakes, valleys and mountains
  • Scenic coach tours
  • Good if the weather is grey
  • Relaxed, low activity

Free things to do

  • Walk the fjord path into the village
  • Visit the 1759 Old Church
  • Follow the Oldeelva glacial river
  • Photograph the ship beneath the mountains
  • Hike to the Huaren viewpoint (steep)
  • Enjoy the waterfalls from the village

Cheap things to do

  • Waffles and coffee by the fjord
  • Brunost and chocolate from the supermarket
  • Olden land train (70 min)
  • Briksdal shuttle bus (from about NOK 575)
  • Loen Skylift (about NOK 650)
  • Kayak or e-bike rental

Day 5 · Wednesday 26 May 2027 · Dress code: Evening Casual

HELLESYLT

Waterfall Village + Geirangerfjord

WATERFALL • UNESCO FJORD • FERRY RIDE • MOUNTAINS • VILLAGE LIFE

THE WATERFALL IS ABOUT THIRTY SECONDS FROM WHERE YOU LAND

WaterfallsUNESCOFerryKayaksCalm

Where the ship docks

  • A 143-metre cruise pier about 200 m from the village centre.
  • There's only one berth. If a second ship calls, it anchors and runs tenders.
  • No terminal building and no transfer bus needed. The village starts at the gangway.
  • The ferry quay is right beside the pier, and there are seasonal tourist info and restrooms.

Can you walk?

  • Yes. The waterfall, ferry quay, shops and café are about 2 minutes on foot.
  • Sunnylven Church is a short uphill walk of about 5 minutes.
  • Apart from the climb to the church, the village is flat.
  • No useful local bus. Inland sights need a ferry, coach excursion or pre-booked taxi.
  • The ferry to Geiranger leaves near the pier, a scenic trip of about 1 hour.

Hellesylt
at a glance

  • Hellesyltfossen~2 min walk
  • Peer Gynt Gallery~2 min walk
  • Sunnylven Church~5 min uphill
  • Swimming areafjord-side walk
  • Norangsdalen~30 min drive
  • Geiranger~1 hr by ferry

  • The one trip that leaves the fjord behind

Day 6 · Thursday 27 May 2027 · Dress code: Evening Casual

HAUGESUND

Homeland of the Viking Kings

VIKINGS • WATERFRONT • SCULPTURES • SHOPPING • WATERFALLS

AN EASY 20-MINUTE WALK OVER THE BRIDGE, OR THE SHUTTLE

VikingsHistoryShoppingCoastArt

Where the ship docks

  • Ships dock at Garpaskjærkaien, a spacious, easy-to-navigate pier.
  • No tender needed, and there are clearly marked areas for shuttle buses and taxis.
  • A combined tourist information desk and souvenir shop opens for every ship.
  • Stalls on the pier sell local excursions and activities.

Can you walk?

  • Yes. It's about 950 m to the centre, roughly a 20-minute walk.
  • The route crosses the town bridge, with great views over Smedasundet.
  • The bridge can feel steep for wheelchair users. Take the shuttle or a taxi instead.
  • Most calls have a shuttle bus that runs continuously while the ship is in.
  • Local buses leave from the town centre, not from the pier.

Haugesund
at a glance

  • Smedasundet~16 min walk
  • Marilyn Monroe statue~18 min walk
  • Haraldsgata~20 min walk
  • Town Hall~22 min walk
  • Haraldshaugen~45 min walk
  • Avaldsnes~25 min by bus

Town Hall & Church

5Haraldshaugen

  • Traditional burial site of Harald Fairhair
  • About 2–3 km north of the centre
  • Walk 35–45 min, or take bus 201

6The Rising Tide

  • Four horse-and-rider sculptures

  • In the sea north of town
  • About 1 hour's walk from the port
  • Check the tide before you go

7Avaldsnes & Viking Farm

  • Waterfall with a 612 m drop into the fjord
  • Scenic countryside drive

  • Spectacular viewpoints
  • A best-seller from the ship
